title: Mass
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 6; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: The tonne is built from things learners know: a 50 kg bag of cement, a 90 kg bag of maize, 20 bags of cement make a tonne. Every t and kg calculation is done in two columns with "1 t = 1,000 kg" written at the top, and the kg column always has three digits.

skills.key_step: The child says that a tonne is 1,000 kg and is used for very heavy things, and chooses g, kg or t by comparing with a known mass.

floor.prerequisite: Chooses g or kg for an object.
floor.question: Which unit for a bag of sugar?

representations: a 1 kg packet of sugar and a 50 kg bag of cement
a picture of a lorry of sand
a unit ladder: g, kg, t
steps: Ask how heavy the object is compared with a 1 kg packet.
Light: g. A person or a bag: kg. A lorry load: t.
Remember 1 t = 1,000 kg.
Mass units are g, kg and t; litres are for capacity.
contexts: a harvest of maize from a cooperative

board.do: Draw a unit ladder with g, kg and t.
Write a goat, a lorry of sand, a pencil.

board.say: Which step of the ladder fits it?

board.do: Wait for the child to choose.
Ask the child to put the other two on the ladder.

misconceptions.ask: How many kg make one tonne?
misconceptions.repair: 1 t is 1,000 kg, heavier than 100 kg.

misconceptions.ask: Can you lift a goat with a few people?
misconceptions.repair: A goat is measured in kg.

misconceptions.ask: Is a goat lighter than a packet of sugar?
misconceptions.repair: A goat is many kilogrammes.

misconceptions.ask: Are we asking how heavy it is or how much it holds?
misconceptions.repair: Heavy loads are measured in tonnes.

checks.question: Which is heavier, 1 t or 100 kg?
Which unit is best for the mass of a lorry load of maize?

skills.key_step: The child picks things heavier than many people together (a lorry load, a heap of sand, a harvest) as measured in tonnes, judging the whole load.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the tonne is for very heavy things.
floor.question: Is a tonne heavier than a kg?

representations: pictures of a cow, a lorry of sand and a crate of soda
how many people would balance the item
a sorting table: g, kg, t
steps: Think of the whole load, not one piece.
Compare with something known: one person is about 50 kg.
If it is like many people or more, use tonnes.
Liquids have mass too.

board.do: Draw a tomato, a crate and a lorry full of crates.

board.say: How many crates fit in the lorry?

board.do: Wait for the child to say many.
Ask which one is measured in tonnes.

misconceptions.ask: Could a few men lift a cow on a stretcher?
misconceptions.repair: A cow is a few hundred kg; a lorry load of sand is tonnes.

misconceptions.ask: Could you carry a lorry of sand on your back?
misconceptions.repair: A lorry load is tonnes.

misconceptions.ask: How many crates are in a full lorry?
misconceptions.repair: Many light things together can make tonnes.

misconceptions.ask: Is a full jerrycan heavy to carry?
misconceptions.repair: Liquids have mass: 10,000 l of milk is about 10 t.

checks.question: Which is measured in tonnes: a goat, a bag of cement or a lorry of sand?
Can a tanker carrying 10,000 l of milk be weighed in tonnes?

skills.key_step: The child uses 1 t = 1,000 kg to say how many equal bags make a tonne by dividing 1,000 by the mass of one bag.
representations: bags of cement stacked to make a tonne
counting in fifties to 1,000
the relation written: 1 t = 1,000 kg
steps: Write 1 t = 1,000 kg.
For bags, divide 1,000 by the mass of one bag.
For a part of a tonne, take that part of 1,000.
Check by multiplying back.
contexts: bags of cement for a school building
sacks of maize at the NCPB depot

board.do: Draw a stack of 50 kg bags.
Count in fifties with the child up to 1,000.
Wait for the child to say how many bags.

misconceptions.ask: How many kg in one tonne?
misconceptions.repair: 1 t is 1,000 kg, so 20 sacks of 50 kg.

misconceptions.ask: Is a tonne only 10 kg?
Can a tonne hold 50,000 sacks?
misconceptions.repair: Divide 1,000 by 50.

misconceptions.ask: How many kg in a whole tonne?
misconceptions.repair: A quarter of 1,000 kg is 250 kg.

checks.question: How many 50 kg sacks make a tonne?
How many kg is a quarter of a tonne?

skills.key_step: The child estimates the whole load by thinking how many tonnes the items make, using a known mass such as 20 bags of 50 kg to a tonne, and says "about".

floor.prerequisite: Knows how many 50 kg bags make a tonne.
floor.question: How many 50 kg bags make 1 t?

representations: a lorry drawn with bags in groups of 20
the groups counted as tonnes
an estimate written with "about"
steps: Find the mass of one item.
Group the items into tonnes (for example 20 bags of 50 kg).
Count the groups.
Say "about" and give tonnes.

board.say: How heavy is one group of 20 bags?

board.do: Count the groups with the child.

misconceptions.ask: Is 2,000 the number of kg or of tonnes?
misconceptions.repair: Divide the kg by 1,000 to get tonnes.

misconceptions.ask: Does the question ask for an exact mass?
misconceptions.repair: An estimate is a round number: about 1 t.

misconceptions.ask: How many groups of 20 bags are in 200 bags?
misconceptions.repair: Ten groups: about 10 t.

misconceptions.ask: Is the lorry as heavy as one bag?
misconceptions.repair: Estimate all the bags together.

checks.question: 40 bags of 50 kg are loaded. About how many tonnes is the load?
A lorry carries 200 bags of 50 kg. About how many tonnes?

skills.key_step: The child multiplies tonnes by 1,000 for kg and divides kg by 1,000 for tonnes, keeping three digits in the kg part.
representations: a place value chart with t and three kg columns
the number with a line three digits from the right
t and kg, and the decimal
steps: t to kg: multiply the tonnes by 1,000 and add the kg.
kg to t: draw a line three digits from the right.
Left of the line is tonnes, right is kg (or after the point).
Check the direction: bigger unit, smaller number.

board.say: How many digits must the kg part have?

board.do: Ask the child to write 045 and join it to the 2.

misconceptions.ask: How many kg in a tonne?
misconceptions.repair: Divide by 1,000: 4.5 t.

misconceptions.ask: Is 3.5 t only 35 kg?
misconceptions.repair: Multiply by 1,000: 3,500 kg.

misconceptions.ask: Is 45 kg the same as 450 kg?
misconceptions.repair: The kg part takes three places: 045.

misconceptions.ask: Should the number of tonnes be bigger or smaller than the kg?
misconceptions.repair: Divide by 1,000: 3 t.

skills.key_step: The child adds kg to kg and t to t, then renames every 1,000 kg as 1 t and adds it to the tonnes.

floor.prerequisite: Adds kg and g with renaming.
floor.question: What is 2 kg 600 g + 1 kg 700 g?

representations: two weighbridge tickets
t and kg columns
the carried tonne written above the t column
steps: Change any amount in one unit so both have t and kg.
Add the kg.
If the kg are 1,000 or more, rename 1,000 kg as 1 t and carry it.
Add the tonnes, including the carried tonne.
contexts: sand for a building in two trips
tea leaves picked in two weeks

board.do: Write 2 t 300 kg + 3 t 900 kg in columns.

board.say: How many tonnes are hiding in it?

board.do: Ask the child to carry 1 t and finish.

misconceptions.ask: Can the kg column hold 1,000 or more?
misconceptions.repair: Rename 1,000 kg as 1 t.

misconceptions.ask: Is 50 kg the same as 5 kg?
misconceptions.repair: Keep three digits in the kg: 050 + 450 = 500.

misconceptions.ask: Where did the tonne from 1,200 kg go?
misconceptions.repair: Add the carried tonne to the tonnes.

misconceptions.ask: Is 3 a number of kg?
misconceptions.repair: Write 3 t as 3,000 kg, then add.

checks.question: What is 2 t 300 kg + 3 t 900 kg?

skills.key_step: When there are too few kg on top, the child renames 1 t as 1,000 kg and takes one off the tonnes.

floor.prerequisite: Subtracts kg and g with renaming.
floor.question: What is 5 kg 200 g - 2 kg 700 g?

representations: a load with some taken off
t and kg columns with renaming shown
a check by adding back
steps: Write the masses in t and kg columns.
If the top kg are fewer, rename 1 t as 1,000 kg.
Take one off the top tonnes.
Subtract kg, then t, and check by adding.
contexts: sand used on a building site
a weighbridge: full lorry minus empty lorry

board.say: Can we take 800 kg from 300 kg?

board.do: Ask the child to cross out 6 t, write 5 t and 1,300 kg.

misconceptions.ask: Which kg are we taking from which?
misconceptions.repair: Rename a tonne when the top kg are fewer.

misconceptions.ask: You used one tonne for the kg. How many tonnes are left?
misconceptions.repair: Take one off the tonnes when you rename.

misconceptions.ask: How many kg in one tonne?
misconceptions.repair: Rename 1 t as 1,000 kg.

misconceptions.ask: What is 1,000 kg - 350 kg?

checks.question: What is 6 t 300 kg - 2 t 800 kg?

skills.key_step: The child multiplies the kg and the tonnes separately, renames every 1,000 kg as a tonne and adds the new tonnes.

floor.prerequisite: Adds t and kg with renaming.
floor.question: What is 2 t 600 kg + 2 t 600 kg?

representations: equal loads on several lorries
t and kg columns, each multiplied
repeated adding as a check
steps: Multiply the kg.
Rename each 1,000 kg as 1 t.
Multiply the tonnes and add the renamed tonnes.
Check by repeated adding for a small number.

board.do: Write 2 t 600 kg x 4 in columns.
Ask the child to rename 2,400 kg and carry.
Write 8 t + 2 t and 400 kg = 10 t 400 kg.

misconceptions.ask: Can the kg column hold 2,400?
misconceptions.repair: Rename 2,000 kg as 2 t.

misconceptions.ask: Does each lorry carry 250 kg too?
misconceptions.repair: Multiply the kg as well.

misconceptions.ask: Where did the 2 t from 2,400 kg go?
misconceptions.repair: Add the renamed tonnes.

misconceptions.ask: How many kg make a tonne?
misconceptions.repair: 2,400 kg is 2 t 400 kg.

skills.key_step: When the tonnes do not share exactly, the child changes the whole mass to kg, divides, and changes back.

floor.prerequisite: Changes t and kg to kg.
floor.question: Write 5 t 400 kg in kg.

representations: a load shared among lorries
the mass changed to kg and divided
the answer checked by multiplying back
steps: Change the mass to kg.
Divide by the number of parts.
Change the answer back to t and kg, or keep kg if asked.
Check by multiplying back.

board.do: Ask the child to write the mass in kg.

misconceptions.ask: What happened to the tonne left over?
misconceptions.repair: Change to kg so nothing is lost.

misconceptions.ask: Is each truck carrying less than half a tonne?
misconceptions.repair: Divide the mass by the number of trucks.

misconceptions.ask: Which unit does the question ask for?
misconceptions.repair: Give the answer in kg: 900 kg.

misconceptions.ask: Are the tonnes shared too?
misconceptions.repair: Divide every part: 8 t / 4 = 2 t.

checks.question: 3 t 600 kg is shared equally by 4 lorries. How many kg does each carry?
